newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Topenergy speeds plans for Russia-Turkey gas link.
newsitem.headline: Topenergy speeds plans for Russia-Turkey gas link.

text.p: Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company Topenergy said on Thursday that it was ready to start an enlargement of a gas pipeline on Bulgaria's territory for transporting Russian gas to Turkey.

Russia's RAO Gazprom, which has a 50 percent stake in Topenergy, is prepared to fund the first part of the construction project, Topenergy board member Sasho Donchev said after a one-day shareholders meeting in Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Varna.
"The remaining funds could be ensured from international lending institutions," Donchev told reporters.

Gazprom's deputy executive director Bogdan Budzuljak said that apart from funding, all problems including "plans and technical studies, land and construction equipment, as well as Bulgarian firms licenced for constructing gas pipelines" were solved.
Topenergy needs to enlarge the network because annual gas supplies to Turkey are expected to be increased from some eight billion cubic metres to 30 billion.
Moscow and Sofia signed in April a long-delayed intergovernmental agreement which involves the transit of Russian gas to the Balkans and construction of new pipelines.

Bulgaria has potential as a gas distribution centre for the Balkans as it has 2,200-km pipeline network, including 625 km of transit pipelines, which receive and transmit gas from outside the country.
